output.brief: FCR fell because of the Finance credit-limit change on 14 April, not mainly because of the new starters. The limit for in-call credits dropped from £100 to £25, and larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The referral share of billing calls rose from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33% and non-referred at 82%, and neither rate changed. Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount as the April intake's, and the referral rate is similar across tenure bands. So the intake, the tariff mix and the IVR redesign look like minor or non-causes. The tariff share of calls rose, but tariff calls still resolve at 85%. I'm fairly confident, though I couldn't directly test workload or the IVR. Don't put the April intake on performance plans; the evidence doesn't support blaming them. Next, agree a revised credit limit with Finance. Pilot it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Then decide on wider rollout. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. The dashboard rebuild is optional and costly.
